# SPD-039 — Bash hook: zsh glob-grouping and numeric-range operators in a redirect target are mis-parsed as shell punctuation

## Brief
SPD-034 makes a captured glob redirect target expand and be checked against every file it opens. But two default-on zsh glob operators in a redirection target -- parenthesised alternation and the angle-bracket numeric range -- are tokenized by shlex punctuation as a subshell or as input/output redirects before expansion runs, so the hook captures the wrong target word and can miss the write. The fault is in the SPD-030 tokenizer, shell_tokens and separate_redirects, not the SPD-034 expander, and it is present on origin/main too. bash rejects both as syntax errors, so it is zsh-only.

Evidence: Probe zsh 5.9 dash-f in a scratchpad. A redirect target using parenthesised alternation of ledger with x, before slash tickets slash SPD-001.md, wrote ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md. A target SPD- then an angle-bracket range 1 to 1 then .md wrote SPD-001.md; the open range wrote SPD-001.md and SPD-002.md. analyse_command captures the target as the absolute fragment /tickets/SPD-001.md for the alternation case and as .md for the range case, both outside the repository, so a double-star member's write is silent. Quoted and POSIX globs are handled by SPD-034; these zsh operators collide with shlex punctuation.
